mainTopic: Selling blemished מעשר בהמה: the rabbinic ban and its exceptions, folding the price into the bones, and the גזירה שוה from חרמים that forbids selling מעשר but not בכור
overview: This amud is about selling the meat of a blemished מעשר בהמה. רבא finishes explaining that by Torah law the meat may be sold. The חכמים banned normal sale, but the ban does not reach parts that are not priced while the animal is alive, and orphans may sell normally. רב שמואל בר רב יצחק agrees, learning it from the פסוק "תזבח ואכלת בשר". רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree about folding the meat's price into the bones, and the גמרא shows they do not really argue. The גמרא then asks why a בכור may be sold but מעשר may never be sold. The answer is a גזירה שוה of ״לא יגאל״ from חרמים, and the גמרא works hard to show that the phrase is "free", why it does not also cover בכור, and why ״הוא״ excludes בכור. Finally, רבא offers a shorter way to show the phrase by חרמים is free, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא finishes his explanation: parts not priced while alive, and orphans
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the חכמים did not extend their decree to parts that are not priced while the animal is alive. For orphans, the חכמים kept the plain Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not make a decree about parts that are not priced when the animal is alive. In the case of orphans, the חכמים kept the Torah law in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבא's statement. He explains why the meat may still be sold by folding its price into the hide, fat, sinews and horns, and why orphans may sell it the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, blemished מעשר בהמה meat may be sold. The חכמים decreed against normal sale. Parts like the hide and sinews do not set the price of a living animal, so the decree never reached them, and that is why הבלעה into them works. For orphans, the חכמים did not want to cause a loss, so they left the Torah law in place and the orphans may sell normally.

keyTerms.meaning: appraised, priced
while the animal is alive
the חכמים made a decree
orphans
they left it standing on Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, blemished מעשר בהמה meat may be sold. The ban is only דרבנן. It does not reach parts that are not priced while the animal is alive, and it does not apply to orphans.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the Torah forbids selling this meat. According to רבא, the ban is only a decree of the חכמים, and that is why it has exceptions.

phrases.english: An item that is not appraised while the animal is alive —

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree does not cover parts that are not priced while the animal is alive, and orphans follow Torah law and may sell normally.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק agrees with רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב שמואל בר רב יצחק agrees with רבא. He asks for the source that orphans may sell their מעשר בהמה in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק also holds like רבא. He asked: From where do we know that orphans' animal tithe may be sold the normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא from another אמורא. This step sets up his question, and the next step gives his answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק says orphans may sell the meat normally, and he looks for a Torah source for it. That only makes sense if the Torah itself allows the sale, which is exactly רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: holds like, agrees with
from where do we know?
the animal tithe
in its normal way

phrases.english: And even Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak
holds like this view of Rava,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: as Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

steps.title: The verse: a blessing only after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק "תזבח ואכלת בשר". The item that has no blessing while alive but does after slaughter is מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Only, with all the desire of your soul you may slaughter and eat meat." Which item has no blessing while alive, only after slaughter? It must be animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק answers his own question with a פסוק. The verse shows that the meat of מעשר בהמה becomes usable, and so may be sold, after it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished מעשר בהמה cannot be sold or redeemed while alive, so it has "no blessing" then. After שחיטה, the verse calls it a blessing, meaning it may be used and sold. Since the Torah itself allows this, orphans may sell it in the normal way, which supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the desire of your soul
blessing; here, usable value
ritual slaughter
you must say, it must be

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah source for selling blemished מעשר בהמה meat is "תזבח ואכלת בשר", read as a blessing that begins only after slaughter.

phrases.english: As it is said: "Only, with all the desire of your soul
phrases.notes: דברים 12:15

phrases.english: you may slaughter and eat meat,"

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ בְּרָכָה מֵחַיִּים
phrases.english: which item has no blessing while it is alive
phrases.notes: The same פסוק goes on to say "according to the blessing of ה׳". Here "blessing" means it can be used and enjoyed.

phrases.english: but only after slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רַק בְּכׇל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question מנין from the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "תזבח ואכלת בשר" refers to מעשר בהמה, which may be used only after slaughter, so it may be sold then.

steps.title: Can the meat's price be folded into the bones?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: may the value of the meat be folded into the price of the bones, the way it may be with the hide, fat, sinews and horns?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the law about folding its price into the bones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the method of folding the price in. This sets up the מחלוקת in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed folding the meat's price into the hide, fat, sinews and horns. The question is whether bones belong on that list too.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them
to fold its price into something else
bones

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about folding it into the bones?
phrases.notes: He means charging for the bones in a way that quietly covers the meat's value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about how far the method of folding the price in can go
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bones can be used, like hide, fat, sinews and horns, to fold in the meat's price

steps.title: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree. One allows folding the price into the bones, and the other forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון son of רבי disagree: one says he may fold it in, and one says he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by recording a מחלוקת. It does not yet say which view belongs to which חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not settled with one answer. It turns into a disagreement between two תנאים, and we are not told who holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: one said
he may fold it in

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi,
one said: he may fold it in,
and one said: he may not fold it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי חַד אָמַר מַבְלִיעוֹ וְחַד אָמַר אֵין מַבְלִיעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by recording a disagreement
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a מחלוקת: one חכם allows folding the price into the bones, and the other does not.

steps.title: No real argument: small animal versus large animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי do not disagree. One is talking about a small animal (דקה) and the other about a large animal (גסה).
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not really disagree. One is talking about a small animal, and the other is talking about a large animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument from Step 5. Each opinion is describing a different kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bones of a small animal are not useful, so nobody buys them. That means you cannot hide the meat's price inside a bone price. A large animal's bones can be made into tools and are sold, so there the meat's price can be folded into the bone price.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not disagree
A small domestic animal, such as a sheep or goat
A large domestic animal, such as a cow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one opinion has been thrown out. Both rulings stay true, each for a different kind of animal.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree
this one is about a small animal
phrases.notes: This is the one who forbids, because small-animal bones are not sold.

phrases.english: that one is about a large animal

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — הָא בְּדַקָּה, הָא בְּגַסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the dispute between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי from Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (אוקימתא): each opinion is about a different type of animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Folding the price is forbidden for a small animal and allowed for a large animal.

steps.title: Another way to reconcile them: local custom
steps.stepSummary: Even if both are talking about a large animal, they still do not disagree. Each rules according to the custom of his own place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say that both are talking about a large animal, and they still do not disagree. Each Sage ruled by the custom of his own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to show there is no real argument. The difference depends on local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In some places people use and sell the bones of large animals, so the meat's price can be folded into them. In other places the bones are not sold, so folding the price is not allowed. The rule depends on whether the bones have a real market in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say instead (introduces another answer)
Both this one and that one
According to his place, meaning the local custom

steps.whatToRemember: Folding the meat's value into the bones depends on whether bones are actually sold. That can depend on the type of animal or on the local custom.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead:
both this one and that one are about a large animal
and they do not disagree
this Sage follows his place

phrases.notes: Each one ruled by whether people in his area sold the bones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reconciliation in place of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local custom: the ruling depends on regional practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe they really argue about a large animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruled by his own locale's custom about selling bones.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: what is the source that מעשר may not be sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a ברייתא: a בכור may be sold, but מעשר בהמה may never be sold. It asks for the source of this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point. About a בכור the פסוק says 'You shall not redeem,' and it may be sold. About מעשר it says 'It shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold, not alive and not slaughtered, not unblemished and not blemished. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ברייתא it quoted earlier so it can study it directly. It asks how we know that מעשר may not be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the phrase ״לא יגאל״ as also forbidding sale. But the plain words only talk about redeeming, not selling. So the גמרא wants to know where the ban on selling comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself; returning to a quoted source to analyze it
Firstborn male animal, given to a כהן
It shall not be redeemed
It may be sold
From where are these words learned?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. 'לא יפדה' is said about a בכור, which may be sold. 'לא יגאל' is said about מעשר, which may not be sold.

phrases.english: Back to the matter itself:
about a firstborn it says: 'You shall not redeem'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:17

phrases.english: and it may be sold;
about the tithe it is said: 'It shall not be redeemed'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33

phrases.english: and it may not be sold,
not alive and not slaughtered,
not unblemished and not blemished.
From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bones discussion and returns to a ברייתא in order to analyze it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that ״לא יגאל״ forbids selling מעשר בהמה

steps.title: The source: a גזירה שוה from חרמים
steps.stepSummary: רב, and also רבי יוחנן, learn this from the shared phrase ״לא יגאל״. Selling is forbidden for חרמים together with redeeming, so the same is true for מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא said in the name of רב, and רב דימי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'It shall not be redeemed' is said about מעשר, and 'And it shall not be redeemed' is said about חרמים. Just as there selling goes together with it, so too here selling goes together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. It uses a גזירה שוה that links מעשר to חרמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חרמים the פסוק says outright that they may not be sold and may not be redeemed. Both topics use the phrase ״לא יגאל״. So the ban on selling carries over from חרמים to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated by declaring it 'חֵרֶם'
Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה)
Selling
A teaching that links two topics through a shared word or phrase

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר בהמה may never be sold. This is learned by a גזירה שוה from חרמים, where selling and redeeming are forbidden together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why מעשר is stricter than בכור, even though both are holy animals that cannot be redeemed.

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana said in the name of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and so too Rav Dimi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
'It shall not be redeemed' is said about the tithe,
and 'And it shall not be redeemed' is said about dedicated property,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28. That פסוק says these things may be neither sold nor redeemed.

phrases.english: just as there, selling goes with it,
so too here, selling goes with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן אָמַר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה built on ״לא יגאל״ in both מעשר and חרמים. Since selling is forbidden with חרמים, it is forbidden with מעשר too.

steps.title: The phrase must be free, or the comparison can be knocked down
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the גזירה שוה only works if ״לא יגאל״ is an extra (free) phrase. Otherwise one could argue that חרמים are different because they apply to everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב הונא son of רב יהושע: The phrase must be free. If it is not free, the comparison can be refuted: חרמים are special, because they can take hold of anything!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a condition to the source from step 9: the shared phrase has to be extra. This sets up the next steps, which try to prove that it really is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גזירה שוה can be broken by showing that the source case has a special strictness the other case lacks. חרמים can be placed on any item, while מעשר applies only to certain animals. So we cannot simply copy the rule from חרמים to מעשר, unless the phrase is ״free″, which protects the גזירה שוה from such arguments.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, extra: a phrase that is not needed for its own place, so it is set aside for a גזירה שוה
Learning a law from one topic to another because the same word appears in both
One can refute it, by pointing out a difference between the cases
They take hold of everything (any item can be made a חרם)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן בר יצחק is rejecting the source from step 9. He agrees with it. He is only saying it needs the phrase to be ״free″ in order to work.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
It must be free, for if it is not free,
phrases.notes: "Free" means the words ״לא יגאל״ are extra in one of these places, so they're left over for the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: one can refute it:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לַחֲרָמִים, שֶׁכֵּן חָלִים עַל הַכֹּל!
phrases.english: What about חרמים? They are special, since they take hold of everything!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְנֵי, דְּאִי לָא מַפְנֵי, אִיכָּא לְמִפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the גזירה שוה given in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of ״לא יגאל״ only holds if the phrase is free; otherwise the special strictness of חרמים could refute it.

steps.title: The phrase in חרמים is extra because we could learn it from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the phrase is free. The Torah did not need to write ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים, because we could have learned it from מעשר. So the phrase is extra and available for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not so, it certainly is free. The Torah could have left out ״and it shall not be redeemed″ by חרמים and learned it from מעשר: just as מעשר is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed. So why did the Torah write ״and it shall not be redeemed″? To make it free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is extra, so the גזירה שוה from step 9 cannot be refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method: if a law by חרמים could be learned from another case anyway, then the Torah's words for it are not needed there. Unneeded words are ״free″ to teach something else, which here is the ban on selling מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Not so
And let it be learned
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
To make it free (for a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: Not so, it certainly is free,
let the Torah not say "and it shall not be redeemed" by חרמים,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

phrases.english: and let it be learned from מעשר:
just as מעשר is holy and cannot be redeemed,
so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed.
"And it shall not be redeemed" that the Torah wrote,
why do I need it? To make it free.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאיֵי אַפְנוֹיֵי מַפְנֵי, לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, וְיִגְמַר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the concern of step 10 by showing the phrase is free
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the phrase is extra because the law could be learned from another case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase by חרמים is needed for its own law, so the גזירה שוה can be refuted
steps.terutzMaskana: The law for חרמים could come from מעשר, so the phrase is free

steps.title: מעשר is stricter, so חרמים cannot be learned from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. מעשר has a special strictness: it becomes holy even on the animal before or after the tenth. So we could not learn חרמים from it, and the phrase by חרמים is needed after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can refute this: מעשר is special, since it becomes holy before it and after it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 11. מעשר is too strict a case to learn חרמים from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn one case from another if the source case has no extra strictness. מעשר is stricter, because a mistaken ninth or eleventh animal also becomes holy. So the Torah had to write ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים, and the phrase is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy before it and after it: the ninth and eleventh animals can also become holy as מעשר by mistake

phrases.english: One can refute this:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁכֵּן קָדוֹשׁ לְפָנָיו וּלְאַחֲרָיו!
phrases.english: What about מעשר? It is special, since it becomes holy before it and after it!
phrases.notes: If he mistakenly calls the ninth or eleventh animal "tenth", that animal also becomes holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁכֵּן קָדוֹשׁ לְפָנָיו וּלְאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חרמים from מעשר, and with it the claim that the phrase is free
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מעשר has a special strictness (holy before and after), so it cannot serve as a source for חרמים

steps.title: The phrase in חרמים is extra because we could learn it from בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new proof. The rule for חרמים could be learned from בכור, which is also holy and cannot be redeemed. So ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is still extra and free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Torah could have left out ״it shall not be redeemed″ by חרמים and learned it from בכור: just as בכור is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed. So why did the Torah write ״it shall not be redeemed″? To make it free.
steps.whatsHappening: After the source from מעשר failed, the גמרא uses בכור instead to show that the phrase by חרמים is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור does not have the ״before and after″ strictness of מעשר, so that objection does not apply. Since חרמים could be learned from בכור, the words ״לא יגאל″ by חרמים are free. They can then teach, through the גזירה שוה, that מעשר may not be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a new approach)
A firstborn kosher animal, holy from birth
Redeemed, made ordinary by paying money

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a proposal: if חרמים could be learned from בכור, ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים would be free. The next step rejects this proof.

phrases.english: Rather, let the Torah not say "it shall not be redeemed" by חרמים,
and let it be learned from בכור:
just as בכור is holy and cannot be redeemed,
so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed.
"It shall not be redeemed" that the Torah wrote,
why do I need it? To make it free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, וְיִגְמַר מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed source (מעשר) from step 11 with בכור, avoiding the objection of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the phrase is extra through a different source case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חרמים cannot be learned from מעשר, the phrase is needed and not free
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: חרמים can be learned from בכור, so the phrase would be free (rejected in the next step)

steps.title: Firstborn is different because it is holy from birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 13. חרמים cannot be learned from בכור, because a בכור is holy from the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about a בכור? It is special because its holiness starts from the womb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last proof. We cannot learn חרמים from בכור, so ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is needed after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy on its own, from the moment it is born. חרמים only become holy when a person sets them aside. Because בכור has this extra strength, a rule about בכור might not carry over to חרמים. So the Torah had to write ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים, and that phrase is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute this; the comparison has a weak spot
What about X? It has a special feature (the standard way of breaking a comparison)
Its holiness comes from the womb, from birth
Firstborn male animal, holy by itself

phrases.english: One can refute this:
What about a firstborn? It is special because its holiness is from the womb!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לִבְכוֹר, שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from בכור given in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חרמים from בכור, so ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is not shown to be free.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בכור is holy from birth, a strictness חרמים do not share.

steps.title: Freeing the phrase by tithe instead, using the word for passing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches sides. ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר is extra, because we could learn from בכור through the shared word ״העברה״ that מעשר cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Torah could have left out ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר, and we would learn it through a גזירה שוה of ״העברה״ and ״העברה״ from בכור: just as בכור is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too מעשר is holy and cannot be redeemed. So why does the Torah write ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר? To make it free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops trying to free the phrase by חרמים and tries to free the phrase by מעשר instead. It says the rule for מעשר could be learned from בכור, so the Torah's words are extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מעשר and בכור use the word ״pass″: by מעשר the animal passes under the rod, and by בכור you ״cause to pass″ the firstborn to ה׳. Through this shared word, מעשר gets the rule of בכור: holy and not redeemable. That makes ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר extra, so it is free for the גזירה שוה with חרמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it not be said; the Torah could have left it out
The shared word ״passing″ that links מעשר and בכור
And one would learn it
To make it free (available for a גזירה שוה)
The Merciful One; the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Two different גזירה שוה are in play. ״העברה״ links מעשר to בכור (no redemption). ״לא יגאל״ links מעשר to חרמים (no selling). This step uses the first to free up the second.

phrases.english: Rather, let it not say "It shall not be redeemed" by tithe,
and one would learn "passing" and "passing" from the firstborn,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:32 (מעשר) and שמות 13:12 (בכור).

phrases.english: just as a firstborn is holy and is not redeemed,
so too tithe is holy and is not redeemed.
"It shall not be redeemed" that the Torah wrote by tithe,
why do I need it? To make it free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 14 failed to free the phrase by חרמים, this step tries to free the phrase by מעשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a phrase is extra because its rule can be learned elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Neither ״לא יגאל״ seemed free, so the גזירה שוה could be broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר is extra, since ״העברה״ from בכור already teaches it.

steps.title: The same refutation works against learning tithe from firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: learning מעשר from בכור has the same weakness, since בכור is holy from birth. So the phrase by מעשר is not free either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, the phrase by מעשר is also not free, because one can refute it the way we refuted before!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new proof with the same argument from Step 14. A בכור is stronger because it is holy from the womb, so maybe מעשר does not get its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בכור is too strong to teach about חרמים, it may also be too strong to teach about מעשר. Then the Torah would need ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר, and the phrase would not be extra. The proof from Step 15 seems to collapse.

keyTerms.meaning: But still; the problem remains
Free, extra (spelled here like מופני)
As we refuted before

phrases.english: But still, by tithe too it is not free,
because one can refute it as we refuted before!
phrases.notes: He means the argument of Step 14: a בכור is holy from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 15 using the refutation from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר is free because מעשר can be learned from בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור is holy from birth, so its rule cannot be passed to מעשר, and the Torah's phrase by מעשר is needed.

steps.title: The word for passing by firstborn is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ״והעברת״ by בכור is an extra word. Because it is free, the comparison cannot be refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall cause to pass" is an extra verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the proof. The word ״והעברת״ by בכור is not needed for anything else, so it is free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the word in a גזירה שוה is extra, we do not break it with a ״מה ל...שכן״ argument. Since ״והעברת״ is extra, מעשר learns from בכור that it cannot be redeemed, even though בכור is holy from birth. That leaves ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר free, so the גזירה שוה with חרמים stands, and מעשר may not be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall cause to pass (שמות 13:12, said of בכור)
An extra verse or word, not needed for its own topic

steps.whatToRemember: The chain: ״והעברת״ by בכור is extra, so מעשר learns from בכור that it cannot be redeemed. That makes ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר extra, so it is free for the גזירה שוה with חרמים, which teaches that מעשר may not be sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of גזירה שוה: an extra word protects the comparison from being broken by a difference between the two cases.

phrases.english: "And you shall cause to pass" is an extra verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 and keeps the proof of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the linking word is extra, so the comparison cannot be refuted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning מעשר from בכור fails because בכור is holy from birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״והעברת״ is extra, so the גזירה שוה from בכור holds and ״לא יגאל״ by מעשר is free.

steps.title: Why not learn בכור from חרמים too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בכור should not also be forbidden to sell, through a 'redemption' גזירה שוה with חרמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us also learn about a בכור, through the shared word 'redemption', from חרמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that a בכור may be sold. It says בכור also has a 'redemption' phrase, so it should be compared to חרמים just like מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר may not be sold because its 'cannot be redeemed' phrase links it to חרמים, which may not be sold. A בכור also has a 'cannot be redeemed' phrase. If the same link works there, a בכור also could not be sold, which contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to the כהן
Let us learn (derive)
Redemption (one of the Torah's words for it)
Property dedicated by a חרם vow

phrases.english: A firstborn too, let us derive
'redemption', 'redemption', from dedications!
phrases.notes: By בכור the פסוק says ״לא תפדה״ (במדבר 18:17); by חרמים it says ״לא יגאל״ (ויקרא 27:28).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing the גזירה שוה for מעשר, the גמרא asks why it does not also cover בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a בכור may be sold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור also has a 'redemption' phrase, so the same גזירה שוה with חרמים should forbid selling it.

steps.title: Only the phrase by מעשר is free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'redemption' phrase by מעשר is extra, but the one by בכור is needed for itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase by מעשר is free; the phrase by בכור is not free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גזירה שוה can only be built on an extra phrase. The phrase by מעשר is extra, but the phrase by בכור is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As shown in Steps 15-17, the rule that מעשר cannot be redeemed is already learned from בכור. So the phrase by מעשר is left free for the link to חרמים. The phrase by בכור is used to teach its own basic law, so it is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe (every tenth animal)
Free, extra; not needed for its own law

phrases.english: That of the tithe is free,
that of the firstborn is not free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Only an extra (free) phrase can be used for a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any 'redemption' phrase could link to חרמים, so בכור would be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the free phrase by מעשר links to חרמים; בכור's phrase is used for its own law.

steps.title: Why not say the opposite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we decide that בכור's phrase is needed and מעשר's is free, rather than the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes you say that 'you shall not redeem' by בכור is for its own law and the one by מעשר is free? Say instead that the one by מעשר is for its own law and the one by בכור is free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 19. It asks why we cannot flip it around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals have a 'cannot be redeemed' phrase, and one could teach the other's law. So we could learn בכור from מעשר and leave בכור's phrase free instead. Then בכור, not מעשר, would be forbidden to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this side over the other?
For itself; teaching its own basic law
To be free (extra) for a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: And what did you see
that 'you shall not redeem' of the firstborn is for itself,
and that of the tithe is to be free?
But say: that of the tithe is for itself,
and that of the firstborn is to be free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only מעשר's phrase is free
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases are equal, so there is no reason to pick מעשר's phrase as the free one rather than בכור's.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה needs the same word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מעשר says ״גאולה״ like חרמים, but בכור uses a different word, ״פדייה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn ״גאולה״ from ״גאולה״, but we do not learn ״פדייה״ from ״גאולה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison must be built on the same word. By מעשר and by חרמים the Torah says ״לא יגאל״, but by בכור it says ״לא תפדה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if בכור's phrase were free, it could not link to חרמים, because the word does not match. Only מעשר shares the exact word with חרמים. So only מעשר is forbidden to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: We judge, we learn one case from another
Redemption (a different Torah word than גאולה)

steps.confusionAlert: Both ״גאולה״ and ״פדייה״ mean 'redemption' in English. The point here is that they are different Hebrew words, and that matters for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: We derive 'geula' from 'geula',
but we do not derive 'pediya' from 'geula'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Word match: a גזירה שוה requires identical words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two phrases are equal, so either could be the free one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מעשר uses the same word (גאולה) as חרמים, so only מעשר is linked.

steps.title: Different words were used in דבי רבי ישמעאל's גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a different word should not matter, since דבי רבי ישמעאל learned a גזירה שוה from ״ושב״ and ״ובא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: ״ושב הכהן״ and ״ובא הכהן״ — returning and coming are the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 21. It brings a case where a גזירה שוה was made from two different words. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a house with צרעת, the Torah says the כהן 'returns' (״ושב״) and later 'comes' (״ובא״). דבי רבי ישמעאל compared these as one, even though the words differ. So ״פדייה״ and ״גאולה״ should also be close enough, and בכור should be included again.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make?
It was taught in the study house of רבי ישמעאל
Returning
Coming

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return', 'and the priest shall come' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, about a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming!
phrases.notes: He means the two words count as the same for the comparison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״פדייה״ cannot be learned from ״גאולה״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דבי רבי ישמעאל made a גזירה שוה from different words with the same meaning, so a word difference should not block the comparison.

steps.title: A matching word beats a different word
steps.stepSummary: Different words can make a גזירה שוה only when there is no exact match. When an exact match exists, we learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule (that the words don't have to be identical) applies only when there is no matching word. But when there is a matching word, we learn from the one that matches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from ״ושב״ and ״ובא״. Different words can link two topics only when nothing better is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רבי ישמעאל used two different words only because nothing closer existed. Here מעשר has the exact word ״גאולה״, just like חרמים, so we link חרמים to מעשר and not to בכור, which says ״פדייה״.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only...
Something that matches it
We learn it (derive it)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject ״ושב״ ״ובא״. It only limits it: different words count only when there is no exact match.

phrases.english: This applies only
where there is nothing that matches it,
but where there is something that matches it —
phrases.notes: Here that means מעשר's word ״גאולה״, which is the exact same word used by חרמים.

phrases.english: we learn from the one that matches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 22 from ״ושב״ ״ובא״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since different words can form a גזירה שוה, בכור's ״פדייה״ should link to חרמים just as well as מעשר's ״גאולה״ does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different words count only when no exact match exists. Since מעשר matches exactly, חרמים links to מעשר.

steps.title: Let בכור learn from מעשר through 'passing'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בכור doesn't pick up the no-selling rule from מעשר through the shared word ״העברה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let בכור learn from מעשר through the word 'passing' that appears by both, since מעשר itself learned the 'redemption' rule from חרמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Even if בכור doesn't link straight to חרמים, it could link to מעשר and pick up the same rule from there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר and בכור both use a form of ״העברה״. So a chain could work: חרמים → מעשר through ״גאולה״, then מעשר → בכור through ״העברה״. That would make the no-selling rule apply to בכור too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Passing' — a word used for both בכור and מעשר
Redemption
Property declared חרם (given to the כהנים)

phrases.english: But let בכור learn
'passing' 'passing' from מעשר,
phrases.notes: בכור: ״והעברת״ (שמות 13:12). מעשר: ״אשר יעבר תחת השבט״ (ויקרא 27:32).

phrases.english: since מעשר also learns
'redemption' 'redemption' from חרמים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that חרמים links to מעשר, then tries to carry the rule onward from מעשר to בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that only מעשר, and not בכור, is forbidden to be sold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second גזירה שוה (העברה) would pass the rule from מעשר to בכור.

steps.title: The word 'it' leaves out בכור
steps.stepSummary: The word ״הוא״ by חרמים limits the rule and leaves out בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah limited it by חרמים with the word 'it' — 'it,' and not בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah itself blocked the rule from reaching בכור. It did this with the extra word ״הוא״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״הוא״ in the חרמים פסוק means 'only this kind'. That exclusion is aimed at בכור, so the chain through ״העברה״ cannot carry the rule to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah limited (excluded)
'It' — a word that limits the rule to this case

phrases.english: The Torah limited it by חרמים with 'it' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28: ״קדש קדשים הוא לה׳״.

phrases.english: 'it,' and not בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24 by pointing to a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that excludes a case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule could pass from מעשר to בכור through ״העברה״.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״הוא״ excludes בכור, so בכור may be sold.

steps.title: Maybe 'it' leaves out מעשר instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״הוא״ shouldn't exclude מעשר instead of בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: 'it,' and not מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know which animal the word ״הוא״ is excluding. Perhaps it excludes מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״הוא״ only says that something is excluded. It does not say what. Without a reason, it could just as easily remove מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead

phrases.english: But say: 'it,' and not מעשר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which case the exclusion in Step 25 is aimed at.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion has no stated target, so it could just as well remove מעשר.

steps.title: מעשר says 'redemption' just like חרמים
steps.stepSummary: מעשר uses the same word ״גאולה״ as חרמים, so it stays included, and ״הוא״ excludes בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר has 'redemption,' just like it (חרמים).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״הוא״ can't exclude מעשר, because מעשר shares the exact word ״גאולה״ with חרמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is the closer match, so it is included. The exclusion therefore falls on בכור, the weaker link. The final result: a blemished מעשר may not be sold, but a blemished בכור may.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like it

steps.whatToRemember: Through ״גאולה״, מעשר is like חרמים and may not be sold. בכור is excluded by ״הוא״ and may be sold.

phrases.english: מעשר has 'redemption,' just like it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means חרמים: both פסוקים say ״לא יגאל״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 by using the matching-word point from Step 21.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר matches חרמים exactly, so ״הוא״ excludes בכור.

steps.title: רבא: 'it may not be redeemed' by חרמים is free to teach
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is not needed for חרמים itself, so it is free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'It may not be redeemed,' said about חרמים, is not needed. For where are they? If they are with the owner, they are הקדש. If they are with the כהן, they are חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new approach. He shows that the phrase ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים has no job of its own, so it can be used to teach about another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the owner, חרמים are הקדש, so they simply follow the laws of הקדש, and the phrase adds nothing. With the כהן, they are ordinary property, so redemption doesn't apply at all. Either way the phrase teaches nothing about חרמים, so it is free to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It may not be redeemed
Not needed (for its own case)
Holy property belonging to the Temple
Ordinary, non-holy property

steps.whyThisMatters: A גזירה שוה is much stronger when its words are free (not needed for their own case). רבא reaches that result directly from חרמים, instead of through the long chain of proofs in steps 11-17.

phrases.english: רבא said:
'It may not be redeemed' of חרמים is not needed,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28.

phrases.english: for where are they?
If they are with the owner — they are holy property,
if they are with the כהן — they are ordinary property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דַּחֲרָמִים לָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a different explanation for the חרמים–מעשר גזירה שוה, showing the חרמים side is free.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים has no use for חרמים themselves, so it is free to serve a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the two stages of חרמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חרמים are like הקדש while still with the owner, and like חולין once given to the כהן. Each half is learned from its own פסוק. This supports רבא's point that ״לא יגאל״ is not needed for חרמים themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: חרמים, as long as they are still in the owner's house, are like הקדש in every way, because the פסוק says, "Every חרם is most holy to ה׳." Once he gives them to the כהן, they are like חולין in every way, because the פסוק says, "Every חרם in Israel shall be yours." So the words "It may not..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא's statement from the last step. It then starts quoting ״לא יגאל״ again, which sets up רבא's next point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no stage at which ״לא יגאל״ would teach us something new about חרמים. With the owner, they already follow the laws of הקדש because of the פסוק ״קדש קדשים הוא לה׳״. With the כהן, they are plain חולין, which he may sell like anything else he owns. Since the words are not needed for חרמים, they are free to be used for a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Items a person dedicates with the word חרם
The owner's house, meaning before the item is handed over to the כהן
Property set aside for the בית המקדש
Ordinary property that is not holy
In every way, for every law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is saying חרמים stop being חרמים. It is describing how they are treated at two different stages: first with the owner, then with the כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא shows that the words ״לא יגאל״ are not needed for חרמים themselves. That is exactly what allows them to be used for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: dedicated items (חרמים),
as long as they are in the owner's house
are like consecrated property in every way,
as it says: "Every dedicated item
is most holy to ה׳."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

phrases.english: Once he gave them to the כהן,
they are like ordinary property in every way,
as it says: "Every dedicated item in Israel
shall be yours."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:14

phrases.english: "It may not..."
phrases.notes: This is the start of the quote ״לא יגאל״. רבא picks his point back up right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in step 28 that ״לא יגאל״ is not needed for חרמים themselves.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that ״לא יגאל״ by חרמים is free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses two פסוקים: חרמים are הקדש while with the owner (ויקרא 27:28) and חולין once given to the כהן (במדבר 18:14).
